title: Advanced I (Word Smart–style)
description: SAT-level words with original learner definitions. Import your own Word Smart 1 list in Settings to add the book's words.

words.definition: to become less strong or intense
examples: We waited for the storm to *abate*.
Her anger slowly *abated*.

words.definition: something that is different from what is normal or expected
examples: His poor test score was an *aberration*; he usually does well.
The cold summer was a weather *aberration*.

words.definition: to choose not to do something, especially something enjoyable; to choose not to vote
examples: He *abstained* from sweets for a month.
Three members *abstained* in the vote.
words.note: abstain FROM something. Nouns: abstinence, abstention.

words.definition: angry and bitter feelings or words
examples: The divorce was full of *acrimony*.
The meeting ended in *acrimony*.

words.definition: refusing to change your opinion or decision
examples: She was *adamant* that she had locked the door.
He is *adamant* about not moving.

words.definition: friendly and easy to talk to
examples: Our *affable* host made everyone feel welcome.
He's an *affable* man with a warm smile.

words.definition: to make pain or a problem less severe
examples: This medicine will *alleviate* your headache.
New subway lines may *alleviate* traffic congestion.

words.definition: having mixed or opposite feelings about something
examples: I feel *ambivalent* about moving to a big city.
She was *ambivalent* about the job offer.

words.definition: something unusual that does not fit a pattern
examples: Scientists noticed an *anomaly* in the data.
A snowy day in May is an *anomaly* here.

words.definition: a lack of interest, energy or concern
examples: Voter *apathy* led to a low turnout.
His *apathy* toward school worried his parents.

words.definition: based on chance or personal choice rather than on reason
examples: The rules seemed *arbitrary* and unfair.
He picked an *arbitrary* number.

words.definition: very plain and simple, without comfort or decoration; strict and serious
examples: The monk lived in an *austere* room.
Her *austere* manner made students nervous.
words.note: Noun: austerity (also: strict cuts in government spending).

words.definition: kind and wanting to help others
examples: A *benevolent* donor paid for the new hospital.
She gave him a *benevolent* smile.

words.definition: honest and direct, even when the truth is unpleasant
examples: To be *candid*, I didn't like the movie.
She gave a *candid* interview about her failures.

words.definition: changing mood or behavior suddenly and without reason
examples: The *capricious* weather ruined our picnic.
A *capricious* boss is hard to work for.

words.definition: so satisfied with yourself that you stop trying to improve
examples: After winning twice, the team became *complacent*.
We can't afford to be *complacent* about safety.

words.definition: very easy to see or notice
examples: He felt *conspicuous* in his bright yellow suit.
There was a *conspicuous* lack of evidence.

words.definition: believing that people act only for selfish reasons
examples: Many voters are *cynical* about politicians' promises.
Don't be so *cynical* — some people really want to help.

words.definition: polite respect for someone's opinions, wishes or position
examples: Students bowed in *deference* to their teacher.
Out of *deference* to her parents, she stayed home.

words.definition: working hard and carefully
examples: She is a *diligent* student who never misses homework.
After *diligent* research, he found the answer.

words.definition: able to speak or write clearly and persuasively
examples: She gave an *eloquent* speech about peace.
His letter was short but *eloquent*.

words.definition: based on observation or experiment rather than theory
examples: We need *empirical* evidence to support this claim.
The study is based on *empirical* data.

words.definition: lasting for a very short time
examples: Fame on social media is often *ephemeral*.
The beauty of cherry blossoms is *ephemeral*.

words.definition: careful not to waste money or food
examples: My *frugal* grandmother saved every plastic bag.
They lived a *frugal* life.

words.definition: enjoying being with other people; sociable
examples: Her *gregarious* personality makes her popular.
Dolphins are *gregarious* animals.

words.definition: acting as if you are better than other people
examples: The *haughty* waiter ignored our questions.
She gave him a *haughty* look.

words.definition: acting quickly without thinking carefully
examples: His *impetuous* decision to quit cost him a lot.
Don't be *impetuous* — think it over.

words.definition: not interested in something or not caring about it
examples: He seemed *indifferent* to her feelings.
The public was *indifferent* to the new policy.

words.definition: clear and easy to understand; able to think clearly
examples: She gave a *lucid* explanation of the theory.
The patient was *lucid* and able to talk.

words.definition: very careful about small details
examples: She keeps *meticulous* records of her spending.
The painting shows *meticulous* attention to detail.
